first_impression.reaction: Good start. It tells us straight away how the ideas are grouped and that there's a section on what changes overseas, which is the bit we actually care about. No fairytale stuff. We skimmed the style headings, then read the practical and destination sections properly.

journey.quote: These wedding place cards ideas are grouped by style, so you can shortlist in a minute: classic paper, natural and edible, keepsakes, glass and acrylic, local touches, and cards that sit on the napkin or plate.
journey.reaction: Respects our time. We can jump straight to the groups we like.

journey.quote: For a destination wedding, decide early whether the cards are made at home and carried or made near the venue, and who sets them out on the day.
journey.reaction: This is the question we wouldn't have thought to ask. Who actually sets them out is exactly the 'no one accountable' worry.

journey.section: Glass, Mirror and Acrylic Place Cards
journey.quote: Mirror marks easily, so ask whoever sets the tables to wear gloves or give each card a final polish.
journey.reaction: Small, specific detail that sounds like someone who's been at a set-up. That's the kind of thing that makes us trust a planner.

journey.section: Keepsake Place Cards That Double as Favours
journey.quote: Shot glasses suit a lively reception.
journey.reaction: Not for us. Feels a bit hens-night next to the marble and calligraphy. Easy to skip, though.

journey.quote: This is general information rather than legal advice, and for a wedding overseas, ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens.
journey.reaction: Half our guests are flying in and the wedding won't be in Australia, so the Food Standards Code part reads like it's for someone else. The overseas line is the one that matters to us and it's tucked at the end after the disclaimer.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events says signage needs to be clear, logical, accurate and accessible.
journey.reaction: Slightly odd to see Queensland government guidance on a place card page, but the takeaway (test it by candlelight, bold ink) is useful.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: If you would like someone to manage the guest list and the vendor briefings with you, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: That's the spreadsheet problem in one line. Soft enough that it doesn't feel like a sales pitch.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Carry finished cards flat and boxed in your hand luggage.
journey.reaction: Practical. Exactly the kind of thing we'd otherwise learn the hard way.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, and works in your time zone.
journey.reaction: This partly answers 'what does end-to-end actually mean'. One person, our time zone. Good.

journey.quote: Once you have a shortlist, you need someone to make the cards.
journey.reaction: Wait, two sections ago the Advisor was our single point of contact for vendors, and now we're finding our own stationer from a directory? It's not clear whether this is for people planning on their own or what happens if we use Concierge. Makes us wonder if we'd end up doing the legwork anyway.

journey.section: Plan the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and fee in writing up front directly addresses our currency and hidden-cost worry. Would still like a ballpark somewhere, but this is reassuring.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what do place cards cost per guest for the different styles (paper vs stone vs glass)? Even a range would help us shortlist.
If we use Wedded Concierge, does the Advisor brief the stationer and arrange who sets the cards out, or do we still do that ourselves?
Are there any real weddings with venue and date where we can see these place cards on an actual table?
What does the Wedded Concierge fee look like, even as a range or how it is structured?

turn_offs_found.quote: Shot glasses suit a lively reception.
turn_offs_found.why: Mildly try-hard for the tone we want; we'd worry about our friends' reaction. Minor.

would_share_with: Mum, who is keen on the calligraphy and keepsake ideas

cta_reaction.quote: If the details are starting to stack up, talk to Wedded Concierge about the wider plan.
cta_reaction.why: Tone is right and the single point of contact plus fee in writing appeals. But this is a place card post and we're 14 months out with no destination. We'd click through to look around, not enquire yet. We want to see a real wedding and a couple more posts first, and the stationer section muddied whether Concierge actually takes this off our plate.

top_3_changes: Clarify the stationer section is for couples organising it themselves, so it doesn't contradict the Advisor being the single point of contact for vendors. Old: "Once you have a shortlist, you need someone to make the cards." New: "If you are organising the cards yourself, you need someone to make them once you have a shortlist."

Put the overseas allergen line before the disclaimer so destination couples see it. Old: "This is general information rather than legal advice, and for a wedding overseas, ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens." New: "For a wedding overseas, ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens. This is general information rather than legal advice."

Tie the closing back to what the page already says the Advisor covers, so the CTA answers 'why would I need help with this'. Old: "Place cards are one small detail of a larger weekend." New: "Place cards are one small detail of a larger weekend, alongside the guest list, the vendor briefings and the travel."
